text.p: SME - Parliament is expected to vote on a resolution asking President Michal Kovac to call a referendum on NATO membership.
- Slovakia's ambassador to the Vatican, Alexander Neuwirth, will return to his post this Friday. Neuwirth was recalled to Bratislava for consultations in April 1996.
NARODNA OBRODA - Parliament on Wednesday approved a law on the protection of non-smokers. The law forbids advertising of tobacco products in all media.
- Private televivion channel TV Markiza said it might bid for the privatisation of the second channel of state Slovak television.
- Hydro-construction firm Vahostav Zilina will issue a 400 million crown tranche of domestic bonds in April.
- The opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) said it had received an invitation for bilateral talks with the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS).
- The public television STV said it would ask the finance ministry for an increase in television fees to some 100 crowns a month from the current 50.

- Major brewery Topvar said its production totalled 560,000 hectolitres in 1996. Topvar exported some 47,000 hectolitres of beer to 18 countries. The company plans to maintain its 1996 production and exports volumes this year.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Legislative Council of the Slovak government on Wednesday rejected a draft law on direct presidential elections, proposed by parliamentary opposition parties.
- Investment fund VUB Invest said it expected a 19.6 million crown pre-tax profit in 1996. The fund manages property worth some 152 million crowns.

PRAVDA - President Michal Kovac welcomed the parliamentry decision to reject the controversial amendment to the penal code, saying its approval would have seriously damaged Slovakia's chances of integration into western structures.
